title: Opened papers do not give one month when joint attention starts
summary: One 2023 review says joint-attention behaviors have been shown from about 6 months, and a 2021 paper says the ability emerges around 9 months.
body: Bradley, Smith, and Wilson write that joint-attention behaviors have been shown to emerge at about 6 months in typically developing children, citing a 2014 chapter this card did not open on its own. Gabouer and Bortfeld write that the ability emerges early, at around 9 months, citing Mundy and colleagues. Both sentences report the literature rather than a new birthday count. This card does not average 6 and 9 into a single onset, and it does not turn either month into a test result.
